Subject: Draft MAP: evaluation success playlist + test protocol

Claire — attaching the working draft of the MAP and a proposed test-case catalog for the eval. High level asks:

- Define "success" in measurable terms (targets we can automate-check) — see Section A in the spreadsheet.
- Confirm exit gates (safety, latency, and accuracy thresholds) and which gate triggers rollback.
- Assign owners for each acceptance test and a 2-week cadence for evidence artifacts.

What I put together: a 6-week evaluation runway with three milestone checkpoints (integration smoke, 50k token warm run, and final concordance). Each checkpoint has pass/fail criteria and a recommended rollback path.

Attachments: Medica_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP with milestone rows), eval-test-cases.md (concrete tests and sample prompts), SLA_addendum.docx (pricing / SLA notes).

Next step: can you review Section A + the security gate rows and tell me which is a hard block vs. negotiable by EOD Thursday? If it's easier, we can take a quick 20m call Thursday morning to walk through.

Thanks,

Jordan — thanks for this. Quick notes after a fast pass:

- Section A success metrics look reasonable; we need a clearer definition for the "concordance" metric (is it micro-avg F1 or case-level pass rate?). Our clinical QA team prefers case-level pass rate at 95%.
- Security gate: SOC-2 evidence and a signed DPIA are hard blocks. The security team here (cc'd) will share the baseline questionnaire by tomorrow.
- Acceptance owners: we can own clinical QA and edge-case signoff; we'll need Redwood to own integration load testing and KV-cache performance measurements.

I'll review the test-case doc in more detail tomorrow and confirm. A 20m call Thursday 10a PT works for us.

Subject: Re: Draft MAP: evaluation success playlist + test protocol — owners & gating decisions

Thanks everyone — short, actionable recap so we have a single source of truth before the call Thursday: 

1) Success definition (final):
   - Clinical concordance: case-level pass rate >= 95% across 500 sampled cases (Medica-owned test set).
   - Latency: p95 generation latency < 350ms at steady-state (Redwood to measure during warm run).
   - Cost tolerance: per-1k-token cost within the agreed budget band in SLA_addendum.docx.

2) Exit gates (hard blocks):
   - Failing SOC-2 questionnaire items marked as "high" by Medica security.
   - Any data-retention noncompliance with Medica policy.

3) Acceptance test owners:
   - Clinical QA & final concordance sampling: Claire / Medica clinical QA team.
   - Integration & load test (50k token warm run): Redwood (Jordan + eng ops).
   - KV-cache / prefix cache validation: Redwood eng ops.
   - Evidence artifacts: owners must upload runbooks and raw logs to the Drive folder in Related Links within 48 hours of each checkpoint.

4) Timing & go/no-go cadence:
   - Week 0 (kickoff): integrate agents; baseline smoke.
   - Week 2: integration smoke — checklist due, go/no-go decision.
   - Week 4: 50k token warm run — performance and cost validation.
   - Week 6: final concordance sampling and signoff.

5) Procurement cadence:
   - Marissa to issue milestone invoice schedule after Medica legal redlines SLA addendum.

Claire — please confirm the SOC-2 baseline questionnaire arrival and whether Thursday 10a PT still works. If everything looks good I'll capture these bullet points into the MAP and push an updated spreadsheet to the Drive.

Hannah
